title: Ownership of Several Ashgrove CareAssure Policies
content:
**New business guideline — Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance**

An owner may hold more than one Ashgrove CareAssure policy of Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance, on the owner's own life or on a spouse's life. There is no maximum number of CareAssure policies per owner: the count is not capped. What is limited is the specified amount on one insured, which is governed by the per-insured aggregate limit on CareAssure coverage.

| Question the rule answers | Answer under this guideline |
|---|---|
| May one owner hold two or more CareAssure policies? | Yes. |
| On whose life may those policies be held? | The owner's own life or a spouse's life. |
| Is there a cap on how many policies one owner may hold? | No; the number is not capped. |
| Is the specified amount on one insured unlimited as a result? | No; it is governed by the per-insured aggregate limit. |

Illustration (hypothetical owner): an owner who already holds an Ashgrove CareAssure 4-Year on her own life and an Ashgrove CareAssure Lifetime on her husband's life is not barred from a further CareAssure policy by the number of policies she holds; whether the further policy can be issued on either insured turns on the per-insured aggregate limit for that insured, not on her policy count.
